candidate_question: Will you support a Data Bill of Rights giving people the right to access, move, delete, and receive a full accounting of their personal data, including prescription, grocery, food, product-purchase, loyalty-program, and other commercial data, and requiring data sellers to update a government ledger to receive safe harbor from liability?
plain_english_frame: Access, move, delete and receive a full accounting of your personal data.
description_text: A commitment to bring U.S. personal data rights closer to strong European-style access, portability, deletion, and accountability standards, while extending those rights to everyday commercial data such as prescription histories, grocery rewards data, food purchases, product purchases, location-linked transactions, loyalty programs, and other consumer profiles. The commitment also asks whether companies that sell or transfer personal data should be required to update a government ledger or registry in order to qualify for safe harbor from prosecution or civil liability.

candidate_question: Will you support a law requiring mandatory review, public reporting, and potential restrictions on U.S. weapons, funding, intelligence, or diplomatic support when credible evidence indicates that support may be connected to war crimes?
plain_english_frame: Mandatory review, reporting and support restrictions when credible evidence indicates war crimes.
description_text: A commitment to require mandatory review, public reporting, condemnation, and potential aid or arms-transfer consequences when credible evidence indicates that U.S. weapons, funding, intelligence, or diplomatic support may be connected to war crimes. The issue should be framed as a universal rule, not a country-specific attack: no blank checks for war crimes by allies, adversaries, proxies, or any armed force.

candidate_question: Will you support a ban on members of Congress, their spouses, and dependent family members trading individual stocks while in office?
plain_english_frame: No trading on the people's trust.
description_text: A commitment to ban members of Congress, spouses, and dependent family members from trading individual stocks while in office, or to require qualified blind trusts and stronger disclosure rules. This can be evaluated through candidate statements, bill sponsorship, voting records, and financial-disclosure signals where available.

candidate_question: Will you support constitutional or statutory reforms to reduce the influence of unlimited outside spending, dark money, and Super PAC power after Citizens United?
plain_english_frame: Reduce corporate/election-money distortion after Citizens United.
description_text: A commitment to support a constitutional amendment, statutory reforms, disclosure rules, public financing, or other measures designed to reduce the influence of unlimited outside spending, dark money, and Super PAC power in elections. candidate_question: Do you support the provision to merge U.S. and Israeli military command structures in the FY27 NDAA (Section 219 in the House bill, formerly Section 224), and why?
plain_english_frame: Section 224 of the FY27 NDAA embeds U.S. forces into Israeli military command structures. Voters deserve to know where their representatives stand.
description_text: Rep. Ro Khanna introduced an amendment to strike Section 224 from the FY27 NDAA during House Armed Services Committee markup. The amendment failed by voice vote, leaving no individual tally on the record. This commitment asks every HASC member to state publicly whether they supported or opposed the amendment and whether they back deeper U.S.–Israel military integration.
